notes.text: The opening paragraph compares the decompositions indexed by two distinct edges. The revised condition is written in the interline and the left margin, using s∈S, order 2, and the three named sets U_s,E_a,E_b. The label is repeated in the slanted marginal note; the verb there remains uncertain. No proof of the opening statement was checked.

The construction paragraph names an arbre topologique, gives a pair involving underlined Gamma and S, and explicitly annotates the underlined Gamma with “esp. top.” It then chooses a point on every edge and writes the barycentric-subdivision pair with S amalg A prime braced as S star. These roles prompted attention to the script X, the stars, the brace, and the relation following A prime; the relation retains the visibly internal stroke as its first candidate.

The NB concerns order-2 vertices in A prime and allocates the two extremities of an edge of script X star between A prime and S. The author writes “voici une description complète”. Reading that description did not constitute a proof check. The exact visible wording une exactement and appartient à was retained.

The last paragraph discusses cutting the underlying topological space at a prime, two connected components, their closures, and binary decompositions. The cancelled s and terminal nt prompted scrutiny of the article; its final stroke remains uncertain and is not supplied from grammatical expectation.

The closing non parallèles is legible. It prompted an ink check of the earlier bien/non group but did not settle it. The final raised-t abbreviation is retained with str, stric and strict alternatives instead of expanding it from meaning.

The first- and second-prime marks in the final comparison were inspected as strokes. The second high group is joined and remains a double/single-prime uncertainty. The opening double quote before équateur has no visible closing partner.

No title, written date, or separate author page number is visible. Pencil 28 is at the bottom-left corner and is transcribed as an archive-number comment. No independent drawing or arrow diagram is present; the curved marks in the upper-left area attach inserted writing.

workflow_feedback: Only the assigned page, its two witnesses, page-specific context/doubt rows, supplied preambles, reader brief, and current notation table were read. No other reader, other page, external research, OCR, text recognition, PDF text layer, or compilation was used.

The whole image was viewed once for layout; each provided half was viewed once line by line, including every agreement, word, sign, correction, margin and number. Nineteen crops were created for loci left open by the halves and viewed once each. No locus received a second crop.

All crop source rectangles were checked numerically against the whole image bounds before creation. Upper-slant crop 01 was rotated -45 degrees and trimmed within that same operation to remove white rotation padding; marginal-condition crop 04 was rotated -16 degrees.

Crop 03 was tight around the crowded opening rewrite. Its lower edge cuts the extreme lower tip of the façon f descender, and its upper edge cuts some tallest contextual tips of the cancelled line. Those extremities had been seen in half a; no second crop was made, and the affected deletion readings remain uncertain. This clipping is explicitly disclosed.

Crop 19 includes the legible abbreviation body and raised t; the extreme upper continuation of its long ascender extends into neighboring-line context. No letter body was supplied from that continuation.
No mathematical proof, independent re-proof, or formal computation was performed. The mathematical content guided listed ink checks only; check_events is empty.

Every listed C doubt ID is represented once in findings, with retained or resolved status. Resolved primary C readings are recorded without treating them as errors. Clear H departures have original-image bounds even when no new crop was warranted.

No drawing or diagram was observed. Insertion leaders are represented by attachment and insertion macros. The lower article is localized to its uncertain ending so the common letters are not duplicated.
